chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"If alms-tax (zakat) were forbidden upon us, it would not be permissible for us to travel to Mecca, because every water source between Mecca and Medina is considered alms-tax."

key_terms.الصَّدَقَةُ: Alms-tax (zakat), specifically referring to the charitable distribution in Islamic law
key_terms.بَيْنَ: Between, indicating the geographical scope of the ruling
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Mecca, the holy city central to Islamic pilgrimage
key_terms.وَالْمَدِينَةِ: Medina, the city of the Prophet, often paired with Mecca in geographical contexts

ai.seo_question: Why are Banu Hashim exempt from paying zakat on water sources between Mecca and Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the legal mechanism of *istighna* (exemption) for Banu Hashim, positing that their right to utilize water sources between Mecca and Medina is intrinsically linked to their status as zakat recipients. It illustrates the Shia juristic view that the prohibition of receiving zakat would logically entail the prohibition of benefiting from assets designated as 'zakat,' thereby reinforcing the continuity of their privilege based on their lineage and spiritual status.
